main_text.head: Ænea machina, intecto igne diffiliens in iaculatoris perniciem. VIII.

p.i: Cernis ut in cælum fuerat qua machina torta,
In sanctos quicunque Dei ruis, impie, servos,
Conatus merces hæc manet Ġna tuos.

page.notes: The woodcut shows a bronze cannon on a carriage aiming upward, with a flame at the muzzle, a smoking fuse, and a man at right holding a lit taper who is being struck by debris. The initial C of the verse is a large woodcut-style letter. The last word of line four is printed as "Ġna" (likely "Ena"/"Dna" misprint) and reads "tuos" in the text; the printed form "Ġna tuos" is uncertain. The heading's "VIII." is a roman numeral. Mottled staining and show-through from the reverse page appear across the lower half.
